gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the hours each combo needs to recharge a half-dead battery. Schumacher's own manual table shows that every 6 A Schumacher combo needs 4 h for a 300 CCA battery and 10 h for a 1000 CCA battery at the 6 A rate, whether it costs $79 or $130. The table assumes the battery is 50% discharged, and the 100 A or 200 A engine-start rating does not change these times. Battery Tender's portable Charge N Start 1100 and 1120 charge at only 1 A, which works out to at least 25 h to put back the 25 Ah a half-dead 50 Ah battery is missing.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. clampandcrank.com's combo roundup (2026-09-29) gives charge time only as words like 'overnight' and 'an all-nighter', with no hours per model. batterytrail.com (2026-10-28) only says the CNS 4120 charges 'four times' faster than the CNS 1100 and 1120, with no hours and no prices. plainprepper.com gives the crank and cool-down rules for the SC1281 and CNS 4120 but no recharge hours. Schumacher's category page, the cited source, would not load (HTTP 429). The Advance Auto SC1309 page, the other cited source, was down for maintenance. ChatGPT's own answer lists amps and price only. The manual chart sits inside the SC1309 and SC1281 manuals that ChatGPT got as uncited results, but there the hours are not tied to a model, a price or a battery size, and none of those pages gives the 1 A versus 6 A comparison.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's plug-in Schumacher picks for someone who needs to bring back a dead battery. It also shows the SC1309's extra ~$50 buys more engine-start amps (200 A vs 100 A) and a bigger 40 A boost, but not shorter refill times: both charge at 6 A, and the SC1281 manual says boost runs only in the first 10 minutes. For someone who wants a portable all-in-one, the Charge N Start 1100 and 1120 ($139.95 / $149.95) are mainly maintainers at 1 A. Only the CNS 4120 (4 A, $179.95, out of stock on the maker's store on 2026-11-13) gets recharge times close to the Schumacher units.

findings.product: Schumacher SC1281 (6 A charge / 30 A boost / 100 A engine start)
findings.label: Hours to recharge a 50%-discharged battery at 6 A
findings.value: Powersports 6–32 Ah: 2–5 h; automotive 300–1000 CCA: 4–10 h; marine 50–105 Ah: 5–11 h
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric SC1281 Owner's Manual, page 8 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: This is the manual's CHARGING TIME (Hours) table, 6 A column: 2/5/4/10/5/11. The footnote says the times assume a 50% discharged battery. Row labels come from the CHARGE TIME section of the Spanish ManualsLib copy (https://manualslib.es/manual/112851/Schumacher-Sc1281.html?page=6, read 2026-11-13), which lists Powersports 6–32 Ah, Automotive 300–1000 CCA and Marine 50–105 Ah. I paired each pair of rows with the low and high end of each range; the extracted text does not label the rows explicitly. Check: 105 Ah × 50% = 52.5 Ah ÷ 6 A = 8.75 h, against 11 h in the table.

findings.label: Hours to recharge a 50%-discharged battery at 6 A

findings.label: Engine-start timing (plug-in units)
findings.value: 2 min pre-charge (5 min below 2 V or in extreme cold); crank ≤7 s; 5 min more charging after a failed start; mandatory 180 s cool-down after repeated cranking
findings.source_title: Schumacher Electric SC1281 Owner's Manual, page 9 (ManualsLib)
findings.note: The SC1309 manual page 10 (https://www.manualslib.com/manual/2409936/Schumacher-Electric-Sc1309.html?page=10, read 2026-11-13) gives the same rules. Shortest time to a start attempt is 2 min with wall power; on a battery under 2 V it is 5 min. plainprepper.com already has these rules, so this is not the new fact.
